title: LOOP × MUSE — 87-feature master registry

statusDefinitions.VERIFIED: Source exists and an automated test that passes today proves the behaviour.
statusDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED: Source exists, but no automated test covers the core behaviour yet.
statusDefinitions.PARTIAL: Some of the behaviour exists; the listed gaps remain.
statusDefinitions.PLANNED: Designed (data, API, UI, security, tests) but not implemented in the application.
statusDefinitions.BLOCKED: Needs an external provider, licence, platform capability or hardware that is not available.
statusDefinitions.NOT IMPLEMENTED: No working implementation and no detailed design yet.

dependencyDefinitions.INFRA: Needs extra infrastructure we control (e.g. a WebSocket channel, a job scheduler).
dependencyDefinitions.PROVIDER: Needs a licensed external provider or API key.
dependencyDefinitions.PLATFORM: Needs a browser or operating-system capability that is not available everywhere.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Intelligence on existing data (low risk, little or no schema change)
Phase 8 — Listening tools (no new tables except bookmarks)
Phase 9 — Playlist tools, sharing and community (needs P5)

phaseGate: All backend tests (npm test) and frontend tests (npm run test:web) pass; npm run roadmap:verify confirms every VERIFIED feature cites a test that passed in that run.

The submitted 64-table baseline is unchanged: node backend/scripts/test-phase2-sql.js shows 0 structural differences, node backend/scripts/roadmap/phase2-data-regression.js shows no submitted row missing except rows removed by designed jobs, and npm run phase3:test passes. (Do not run npm run db:phase2 for this: it regenerates the submitted files.)

The promoted proposed migration passes npm run roadmap:test-migration (fresh install, re-run, partial states, interrupted runs, drift, grants) and npm run roadmap:mutation catches every listed mutation.
npm run roadmap:check passes (no reference to a table, route, screen or test that does not exist).

The migration is reviewed by a second person, then copied from proposed/ to database/migrations/ under its number and applied with npm run db:migrate — never edited after it has been applied anywhere.

features.name: LOOP Listening Rooms
features.summary: A host plays a shared queue to invited listeners in real time.

newDb.why: A room has its own lifecycle, members with roles and an ordered shared queue; no existing table models a shared session (listening_sessions belong to one user).

frontend: Room screen with shared Now Playing, member list and queue
Clear 'not synced' state when the connection drops
security: Only the host or a co-host changes playback state
INVITE_ONLY rooms require membership
state_version rejects stale updates (optimistic concurrency)
Each member's own play is recorded in their own history only if they are not in a private session

proposed: non-member cannot read or join an invite-only room (403)
listener cannot change playback state (403)
stale state_version is rejected (409)
LIVE room without started_at is rejected by the database
member in a private session leaves no permanent history

outstanding: A real-time channel (SSE or WebSocket) and its hosting
Synchronised playback is limited to songs with a permitted audio source; metadata-only songs cannot be played together

features.name: Collaborative Playlists
features.summary: Invite editors and viewers to a playlist; see who added what.

newDb.why: Membership with a role is a M:N between users and playlists; version enables optimistic locking for concurrent edits; added_by records authorship.

api: If-Match: version on every playlist write
frontend: Conflict message when the playlist changed meanwhile
security: Only the owner manages collaborators
VIEWERs cannot write
Existing private-by-default behaviour stays the default (visibility PRIVATE)

existing: playlists are private to their owner
proposed: owner invites an editor; editor adds a song; added_by is recorded
viewer cannot add songs (403)
stale version is rejected (409)
ACCEPTED invitation without accepted_at is rejected by the database

Returns only overlap categories, never the other user's history
Not available in private sessions

proposed: refused unless both users consent (403)
score is symmetric for A–B and B–A
users with no preferences get 'not enough data', not 0 %
